ontology.name: membrane
ontology.definition: A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

ontology.name: cAMP binding
ontology.definition: Binding to cAMP, the nucleotide cyclic AMP (adenosine 3',5'-cyclophosphate).

ontology.name: cGMP binding
ontology.definition: Binding to cGMP, the nucleotide cyclic GMP (guanosine 3',5'-cyclophosphate).

ontology.name: photoreceptor outer segment membrane
ontology.definition: The membrane surrounding the outer segment of a vertebrate photoreceptor.

ontology.name: intracellularly cAMP-activated cation channel activity
ontology.definition: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a cation by a channel that opens when intracellular cAMP has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

ontology.name: intracellularly cyclic nucleotide-activated monoatomic cation channel activity
ontology.definition: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a monoatomic cation by a channel that opens when intracellular cyclic nucleotide has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

ontology.name: intracellularly cGMP-activated cation channel activity
ontology.definition: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a cation by a channel that opens when intracellular cGMP has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

ontology.name: monoatomic ion channel activity
ontology.definition: Enables the facilitated diffusion of a monoatomic ion (by an energy-independent process) by passage through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel without evidence for a carrier-mediated mechanism. May be either selective (it enables passage of a specific ion only) or non-selective (it enables passage of two or more ions of same charge but different size).

ontology.name: calcium ion transmembrane transport
ontology.definition: A process in which a calcium ion is transported from one side of a membrane to the other by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

ontology.name: plasma membrane
ontology.definition: The membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cell from its external environment. It consists of a phospholipid bilayer and associated proteins.

ontology.name: protein binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a protein.

ontology.name: intracellular cyclic nucleotide activated cation channel complex
ontology.definition: A protein complex that forms a transmembrane channel through which cations ions may pass in response to an intracellular cyclic nucleotide binding to the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

ontology.name: sodium ion transport
ontology.definition: The directed movement of sodium ions (Na+) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

ontology.name: monoatomic ion transport
ontology.definition: The directed movement of a monoatomic ion into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Monatomic ions (also called simple ions) are ions consisting of exactly one atom.

ontology.name: calcium ion transport
ontology.definition: The directed movement of calcium (Ca) ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

ontology.name: photoreceptor outer segment
ontology.definition: The outer segment of a vertebrate photoreceptor that contains a stack of membrane discs embedded with photoreceptor proteins.

ontology.name: monoatomic cation transmembrane transport
ontology.definition: The process in which a monoatomic cation is transported across a membrane. Monatomic cations (also called simple cations) are positively charged ions consisting of exactly one atom.

ontology.name: sodium ion transmembrane transport
ontology.definition: A process in which a sodium ion is transported from one side of a membrane to the other by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

ontology.name: transmembrane transport
ontology.definition: The process in which a solute is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other.

ontology.name: rod photoreceptor outer segment
ontology.definition: The outer segment of a vertebrate rod photoreceptor that contains sealed membrane discs that are not connected to the ciliary membrane and containing rhodopsin photoreceptor proteins.

ontology.name: sensory perception of chemical stimulus
ontology.definition: The series of events required for an organism to receive a sensory chemical stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. This is a neurological process.

ontology.name: visual perception
ontology.definition: The series of events required for an organism to receive a visual stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Visual stimuli are detected in the form of photons and are processed to form an image.

paint_node_review.interpretation: The current v19 topology places CNGA1 below the recorded IBD gain and outside the recorded SF6 loss branch. The preserved 20250408 node assertions support the inherited target annotation; the SF6 loss cannot be projected onto SF9. No original curator alignment session or residue-level loss rationale was recovered. Current aligned sequences are available, but no chemosensory-specific residue determinant is asserted. GO-slim annotation lists in the tree response are not used as complete GOA inventories.

review.summary: Retain the inherited chemical-sensory context outside the representative rod core.
review.reason: The saved PTHR45638 PAINT records place GO:0007606 at bilaterian node PTN000025806 (IBD, 20250408) and record its loss at PTN002900733 (IRD, same date). The inspected PANTHER v19 tree places human CNGA1/P29973 below the gain in SF9, outside that loss branch; human CNGA3/Q16281 lies within the SF6 loss branch. Thus the cone-subfamily loss is a useful comparator but does not establish loss in rod CNGA1. Retain the positive curated inheritance outside the independently established rod visual core. Rod expression and intracellular cyclic-nucleotide recognition do not independently demonstrate either chemosensory function or its exhaustive absence. The original curator session and residue-level loss rationale were not recovered; no direct human chemosensory assay is claimed.

source_entities.comment: PTN000025806 carries the explicit GO:0007606 IBD assertion. The current family tree places the sequence-authenticated P29973 leaf PTN002469207 below that node and outside the recorded PTN002900733/SF6 loss. This supports the existing curated transfer, not a newly established human chemosensory experiment. The available node records and current tree/alignment replace the earlier unresolved-placement statement; they do not reconstruct the historical curator rationale.
